2027-06-28.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The calendar gives the weekday readings of the Seventh Monday of the Apostles and the readings of the commemoration of Saint Irenaeus; both sets are shown here (verify locally which are read). The Latin Church keeps the memorial of St Irenaeus today, and in the evening celebrates the Vigil Mass of Sts Peter and Paul.
2027-06-28.verse: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.
theo: On the eve of the feast of Peter and Paul the Church remembers a bishop who loved the apostles' teaching more than his own life, and who handed it on so faithfully that he is called today the Doctor of Unity. Irenaeus was born in Asia Minor, probably at Smyrna, in the first half of the second century. As a boy he listened to Polycarp, the bishop of Smyrna, who had known the apostle John. Many years later Irenaeus wrote to a friend that he could still remember the place where Polycarp sat when he taught, how he went in and out, and how he spoke of his conversations with John and with others who had seen the Lord. That is a chain of only three links between Irenaeus and Jesus: the Lord, the beloved disciple, Polycarp, Irenaeus. He went to Gaul, served as a priest in Lyons, and after the persecution of 177, in which the old bishop Pothinus died in prison, he became bishop of that Church. He wrote five books against the false teachings of his day, usually called Against Heresies, and a shorter work, the Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching. When a dispute about the date of Easter threatened to divide the Church of Rome from the Churches of Asia, he wrote to Pope Victor asking for patience and peace; the historian Eusebius says that he lived up to his name, which means peacemaker. He died around the year 200 and has long been honoured as a martyr, though the details of his death are not known. In 2022 Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church, with the title Doctor of Unity.

The readings chosen for him speak of the priest and the teacher. In Exodus the high priest Aaron wears the breastpiece engraved with the names of the twelve tribes: “So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment on his heart when he goes into the holy place, for a continual remembrance before the Lord.” A true shepherd carries his people on his heart into the presence of God. Malachi recalls God's covenant with Levi and describes the priest as God wanted him: “True instruction was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips. He walked with me in integrity and uprightness, and he turned many from iniquity. For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.” Irenaeus was such a priest: he guarded knowledge, not secret knowledge for a few, but the public faith of the whole Church.

Paul's words to Timothy could be Irenaeus' own motto: “But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it.” The Gnostic teachers of the second century claimed to possess secret knowledge passed down privately, and they despised the body, the created world and the God of the Old Testament. Irenaeus answered that the apostles had hidden nothing: their teaching is public, kept in the Churches they founded, and handed on by the bishops who succeeded them. He listed the bishops of Rome, “the very great, very ancient and universally known Church founded and organised at Rome by the two most glorious apostles, Peter and Paul” (in substance), and said that every Church must agree with it because of its preeminent authority. So tomorrow's feast and today's saint belong together. He defended the goodness of creation and of the flesh, which the Son of God took from the Virgin Mary; he saw Mary as the new Eve, whose obedience untied the knot of Eve's disobedience; he taught that Christ sums up and renews the whole of human history in himself. And he gave us the sentence that sums up his joy: the glory of God is the human being fully alive, and the life of the human being is the vision of God. He knew that the Spirit was the guarantee of this teaching, as Jesus promised in today's Gospel: “the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.” All scripture, Paul adds, “is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness.”

The weekday readings fit the peacemaker well. Paul writes about a member of the Corinthian Church who had caused great pain and been punished by the community. Now Paul asks for mercy: “so now instead you should forgive and console him, so that he may not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow. So I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.” Discipline in the Church is never meant to crush, only to heal; and an unforgiving community gives the devil an opening: “we do this so that we may not be outwitted by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his designs.” In the Gospel the scribes and Pharisees ask Jesus for a sign. He gives them only the sign of Jonah, three days in the belly of the sea monster, a sign of his own death and resurrection, and he reminds them that the people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching and that the queen of the South came “from the ends of the earth to listen to the wisdom of Solomon, and see, something greater than Solomon is here!” Irenaeus, who carried the Gospel from Asia to the far west of the empire, and we in India, who received it from Mar Thoma at the eastern edge of the known world, know what it means to come from the ends of the earth to hear the One who is greater than Solomon. Let us listen, repent, forgive, and continue in what we have learned.
outline: A chain of three links: Jesus, John, Polycarp, Irenaeus; and the chain that reaches us.
The priest who carries his people before God, and whose lips guard knowledge.
Point 2 · Continue in what you have learned
Public tradition against secret knowledge; the Churches of the apostles; the Spirit who reminds.
The peacemaker; discipline that heals; something greater than Jonah.
“Continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it.”
live: Know from whom you learned (2 Timothy 3:14)
Thank God today by name for the people who handed on the faith to you: parents, grandparents, catechism teachers, priests; if one is living, call or visit them this week.
Think of one person who has hurt you or the community and has been made to feel it. Find a way this week to console them and show that they are still loved.
fathers: The tradition of the apostles, made known in the whole world, can be seen in every Church by all who wish to see the truth. We can name those whom the apostles appointed as bishops in the Churches, and their successors down to our own time. The apostles, like a rich man depositing money in a bank, placed in the Church in fullness everything that belongs to the truth.

The glory of God is the human being fully alive, and the life of the human being is the vision of God. If the revelation of God through creation gives life to all who live on earth, much more does the manifestation of the Father through the Word give life to those who see God.

When Victor, bishop of Rome, wished to cut off the Churches of Asia over the date of Easter, Irenaeus wrote to him on behalf of the brethren in Gaul, urging him to keep peace with those who held to an ancient custom. So he lived up to his name, a peacemaker in name and in deed.
magis: In order that the full and living Gospel might always be preserved in the Church, the apostles left bishops as their successors, handing over to them their own position of teaching authority.

The glory of God consists in the realisation of his manifestation and communication of his goodness; as St Irenaeus says, the glory of God is man fully alive, and the life of man is the vision of God.
As St Irenaeus says, being obedient Mary became the cause of salvation for herself and the whole human race; the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience.
The Eucharist is the sum and summary of our faith: our way of thinking is attuned to the Eucharist, and the Eucharist in turn confirms our way of thinking (St Irenaeus).
saints: Saint Irenaeus (about 130–about 202), bishop of Lyons, martyr and Doctor of the Church (declared Doctor of Unity by Pope Francis in 2022). In the Latin calendar, his memorial, and in the evening the Vigil Mass of Sts Peter and Paul.

25–30 June: sixth and seventh weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Sun 27: Seventh Sunday of the Apostles, the last Sunday of the season. Mon 28: St Irenaeus, bishop and martyr (also a memorial in the Latin calendar). Tue 29: St Peter and St Paul, the Apostles, an important feast and a day of obligation. Wed 30: in the Latin calendar, the First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church. Looking ahead: the Dukhrana of St Thomas, our Father in faith, on Saturday 3 July, and the Season of Kaitha (Qaita) from Sunday 4 July.
2027-06-28.prayer: Lord God, you gave your Church the bishop Saint Irenaeus to guard the faith of the apostles and to make peace among your people. Through his prayers keep us faithful to what we have learned and firmly believed, and grateful to those from whom we learned it. Give our bishops and priests the heart of Aaron, to carry your people before you, and the lips of a true priest, to guard knowledge and to teach. Send us the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, to teach us everything and to remind us of all that your Son has said. Make us quick to forgive and console, so that Satan may not outwit us, and let us live fully, for your glory, until we see you face to face. Through Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: St Irenaeus wrote that our way of thinking is attuned to the Eucharist, and the Eucharist confirms our way of thinking. At this altar the faith of the apostles is not only taught but celebrated and received: the Body of Christ, which he took from the Virgin, nourishes our bodies for the resurrection. Here the glory of God makes us fully alive.

quick: St Irenaeus, who heard Polycarp, the disciple of John, guarded the public faith of the apostles and made peace in the Church; he is the Doctor of Unity.
His readings: the priest bears the names of Israel on his heart; the lips of a priest guard knowledge; continue in what you have learned; the Spirit will remind you of all that Jesus said.
Weekday: Paul asks the Corinthians to forgive and console the offender; Jesus offers the sign of Jonah, for something greater than Jonah is here.
2027-06-28.action: Thank God by name for those who handed on the faith to you, and console someone who needs to know they are still loved.
2027-06-28.question: Do I continue in what I have learned, or do I chase new and secret teachings?
kidsaint: When Irenaeus was a boy, he listened to an old bishop called Polycarp, who had known Saint John, the friend of Jesus. So Irenaeus heard about Jesus from someone who had heard it from Jesus' own friend! He became a bishop in France and wrote books to protect the true faith, and he helped people who were quarrelling to make peace. His name means peaceful. Lesson: listen to those who teach you about Jesus, and be a peacemaker!
term: The handing on of the apostles' mission and authority through the bishops, from the apostles to the present day, by the laying on of hands. St Irenaeus pointed to the lists of bishops in the Churches founded by the apostles as a guarantee that the Church teaches what the apostles taught.

family.explain: Saint Paul told Timothy: keep what you learned, and remember who taught you. Timothy had learned the Bible as a child from his grandmother and mother. Saint Irenaeus learned about Jesus from Polycarp, who learned from Saint John, who knew Jesus. The faith comes to us through a long chain of people who love Jesus, and the Holy Spirit helps us remember everything Jesus said.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents, parents, catechism teachers and priests, who taught us the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught each of us to pray? Let us thank God for them by name.”

illus: In a parish in Kuttanad (a story told to illustrate the reading) an old catechism teacher was asked by a sharp boy in her class, ‘Teacher, how do we know that what you teach is really what Jesus said?’ She did not answer at once. The next Sunday she brought a long paper chain and hung it across the classroom. On the first link she had written her own name. On the next, the name of the priest who had taught her; then the bishop who had ordained him; then, link by link, the bishops of the Church back through the centuries, until the last links read ‘the Apostles’ and ‘Jesus’. ‘I did not invent this faith,’ she said. ‘I received it, and now I give it to you. One day you will add your link.’ Many years later, that boy, now a priest, told the story at her funeral and said, ‘She taught me what St Irenaeus taught: continue in what you have learned, knowing from whom you learned it.’

pm.open: Holy Spirit, Advocate sent by the Father, you teach us everything and remind us of all that Jesus said. With St Irenaeus we gather to listen; keep us in the faith of the apostles and make us peacemakers. Amen.
share: So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel… on his heart (Exodus 28:29). Whom do I carry on my heart before God?
The lips of a priest should guard knowledge (Malachi 2:7). How do I pray for and support our priests?
Continue in what you have learned… knowing from whom you learned it (2 Timothy 3:14). Who handed on the faith to me?
You should forgive and console him (2 Corinthians 2:7). Whom do I need to forgive and comfort?
pm.resp: Holy Spirit, remind us of all that Jesus said.
interc: For the Church, that she may remain one in the faith of the apostles, through the prayers of St Irenaeus, Doctor of Unity.
For our bishops and priests, that they may carry their people on their hearts and teach the faith with integrity.
For catechism teachers and parents, who hand on the faith to the next generation.
For those who have been hurt in the Church and those who have caused hurt, that forgiveness and consolation may heal them.
For Christians separated from one another, that they may be reconciled in truth and love.
pm.close: Father, through St Irenaeus you kept your Church faithful to the teaching of the apostles. Keep us in that faith, make us peacemakers, and let us live fully for your glory until we see you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Saint Irenaeus, a bishop of the second century. As a boy he listened to Polycarp, who had known the apostle John, who had known Jesus. Think of it: only a few links between Irenaeus and the Lord.

False teachers in his time said that they had secret knowledge that ordinary Christians did not have. Irenaeus answered: the apostles hid nothing. Their teaching is public, kept in the Churches they founded and handed on by the bishops who came after them. Paul says the same to Timothy: “continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it” (2 Timothy 3:14).

The readings for his feast describe a true priest. Aaron carried the names of the tribes on his heart before God. Malachi says, “the lips of a priest should guard knowledge” (Malachi 2:7). And Jesus promises the Holy Spirit, who “will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you” (John 14:26).

Irenaeus was also a peacemaker; his name means peaceful. When a quarrel about the date of Easter threatened to divide the Church, he begged for patience. In the weekday reading Paul too asks for mercy: forgive and console the one who did wrong, reaffirm your love for him, so that Satan may not outwit you (2 Corinthians 2:7–11).

Irenaeus wrote: the glory of God is the human being fully alive. Tomorrow we celebrate Peter and Paul, the apostles whose Church in Rome Irenaeus honoured. Today let us thank God for those who handed on the faith to us, let us forgive, and let us continue in what we have learned. Amen.
kids: Children, Saint Irenaeus heard about Jesus from an old bishop who had known Saint John, Jesus' friend. The faith came to him like a chain, from hand to hand. Today, say thank you to the person who taught you to pray. And be a peacemaker, like Irenaeus!

intro: Theme: “But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.”
On the commemoration of St Irenaeus: the shepherd who carries his people on his heart, the faith that is received and handed on, the mercy that forgives and consoles, and the One greater than Jonah.

q: So have no fear; I myself will provide for you and your little ones.” In this way he reassured them, speaking kindly to them.
so now instead you should forgive and console him, so that he may not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
points.apply: Console one person this week who has been made to feel the weight of their wrongdoing.

q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Make one concrete act of repentance this week instead of asking God for signs.

q: So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment on his heart when he goes into the holy place, for a continual remembrance before the Lord.
“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for your bishop and your parish priest by name.

points.h: Continue in what you have learned
q: For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.
points.apply: Thank God by name for those who handed on the faith to you, and contact one of them.

concl: St Irenaeus received the faith from those who knew the apostles and handed it on whole; he made peace in the Church.
Let us forgive and console, repent at the word of the One greater than Jonah, and continue in what we have learned.
2027-06-28.resolve: This week, console someone, make one act of repentance, pray for your shepherds by name, and thank those who taught you the faith.
